Where does my salary go?

Germany · 2026 rules · enter your gross pay and see every euro's destination

Rules & rates as of Nov 2026

1Your income
Compare your salary
Wage-adjusted (recommended): your salary is scaled by the average wage of that year (Deutsche Rentenversicherung), so you compare a person in the same position. Inflation-adjusted: scaled by consumer prices (Destatis) – same purchasing power. Same euros: no scaling – useful if you enter what you actually earned back then. Only wage-adjusted shows ‘bracket creep’ (kalte Progression).

Your monthly pay before any deductions – the 'Gesamtbrutto' on your payslip or the salary in your contract divided by 12. You can also switch to “/ year” and enter your annual salary – it is divided by 12. Leave out one-off bonuses: a 13th salary is taxed a little differently, so including it only approximates.

Take-home pay is only an estimate until you set tax class, state, children and health insurance below.

2About you
From age 23, people without children pay an extra 0.6% care-insurance surcharge. Untick if you're younger than 23.
Shown on your payslip as 'St.Kl.' or in ELSTER. I: single. II: single parent living with a child. III: married, the higher earner (spouse in V). IV: married, similar incomes. V: married, the lower earner. VI: a second job alongside your main one – no tax-free allowance. A mini-job up to €603 is taxed separately and doesn't count here.
Where you live or work. It sets the church-tax rate (8% in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, 9% elsewhere) and, in Saxony, employees pay a higher share of care insurance.
Tick only if you're a registered member of a church that levies church tax (e.g. Catholic or Protestant). Your payslip shows it under 'Konfession' – '--' means no.
Children you receive child benefit (Kindergeld) for. They remove the 0.6% childless surcharge on care insurance, lower it further from the 2nd child under 25, and reduce solidarity surcharge and church tax. They don't lower income tax itself – families get Kindergeld instead.
3Your insurance
Decides which social insurance you pay. Employee: all four (health, care, pension, unemployment). Working student (enrolled, max. 20 h/week in term): pension only. Civil servant (Beamter): none – the state provides pension and covers part of medical costs.
Most employees are in public health insurance; care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) is always included with it. Private is possible for employees only above €6,450/month (2026), and is usual for civil servants. With private insurance, care insurance is part of your premium.
Pick your public health insurer – the extra contribution (Zusatzbeitrag) is filled in automatically. Can't find it? Choose 'Other' and type the rate from your insurer's website or payslip. Not sure at all? Use the 2026 average.
On top of the general 14.6%, every public health insurer charges its own extra rate. Average for 2026: 2.9%. You pay half. Find yours on your insurer's website.

Using extra contribution: 2.9 % · rates as of Nov 2026

Your total monthly private health + care premium. Employees: the employer pays half, up to €613.22 per month (2026). Civil servants get no employer share – the state's Beihilfe covers part of the medical bills instead.

You pay health, care, pension and unemployment insurance – all mandatory.

4Advanced (optional – tax allowance, company pension, factor method, second job)
An allowance the tax office registered for you on request (Lohnsteuerermäßigung), e.g. for high commuting or work costs. It appears on your payslip as 'Freibetrag'. It lowers your monthly wage tax.
Part of your gross goes straight into a company pension (betriebliche Altersversorgung). Up to €676/month is tax-free and up to €338/month free of social insurance (2026). Your employer must add 15% of the converted amount if it saves contributions.
Alternative to III/V for married couples: both are in class IV, but the tax is multiplied by a factor below 1 so the monthly tax already reflects joint taxation (splitting). Needs your spouse's gross. Applied for at the tax office; it switches your class to IV here.

A job alongside your main one. Up to €603/month it's a mini-job: flat-taxed separately and mostly contribution-free. Above that it's taxed in class VI (no tax-free allowance) and adds to your social insurance.

What happens to the taxes next

Your income tax is collected by the state tax office and split by the constitution (Art. 106 GG). Figures in the boxes are your share. Click any box for an explanation.

How is this calculated?

Income tax follows the official 2026 wage-tax algorithm (BMF Programmablaufplan): 2026 tariff with a €12,348 tax-free allowance, €1,230 employee allowance, €36 special-expenses allowance, and a pension/health/care allowance (Vorsorgepauschale). Class II adds the single-parent relief (€4,260 + €240 per further child). Classes V and VI use the special V/VI formula. Spot checks against published 2026 tables match to the cent (e.g. €3,000 class I → €293.08).

Solidarity surcharge: 5.5%, only once annual income tax exceeds €20,350 (class III: €40,700), with a phase-in zone. Church tax: 8% in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, 9% elsewhere. Children reduce Soli and church tax via child allowances, not income tax itself.

Social insurance (employee share): health 7.3% + half the insurer's extra contribution; care 1.8% (Saxony 2.3%) + 0.6% if childless and 23 or older, −0.25% per child from the 2nd to the 5th; pension 9.3%; unemployment 1.3%. Ceilings: €5,812.50 (health/care) and €8,450 (pension/unemployment) per month. Transition zone €603.01–2,000 uses the official reduced-base formula.

Status: working students pay pension insurance only; civil servants pay no social insurance. Private health insurance: your premium minus the employer subsidy (half, max €613.22/month; none for civil servants), also used for the tax allowance.

Advanced: the personal allowance lowers taxable income; salary conversion is tax-free up to €676 and contribution-free up to €338 per month, with a 15% employer subsidy; the factor method uses the official formula (joint splitting tax ÷ sum of both class-IV taxes, rounded down to 3 decimals; your spouse is assumed publicly insured); a second job up to €603 is a mini-job (2% flat tax, 3.6% pension unless exempt), above that class VI with social insurance on the combined pay. Health insurer rates: 2026 extra contributions as published by the insurers, including changes during the year up to November 2026.

Not included: company pensions, benefits in kind, tax-free allowances on your ELStAM, the factor method, and anything you claim in your annual tax return. This is an estimate for understanding – not tax or legal advice. Your payslip is what counts.

Tax differences between federal states

Income tax and social insurance are the same everywhere in Germany. Only two things differ by state: church tax (if you're a member) and, in Saxony, employees' share of care insurance. Click a state to select it.
